title: Python
theory: Keep the reasoning, change the language
Python lets you express many tasks without manually managing allocations. You still need explicit requirements, correct types, and tests. input returns text; convert deliberately before calculating.

A function returns information to its caller; print displays it. Separate calculation from interaction when you need to reuse or test the calculation. Avoid changing caller-owned collections unless that is part of the contract.

Catch the exception you expect at the boundary where it matters. Do not swallow every error and pretend the program worked. State how invalid input, empty collections, and malformed records should behave.

Use files and standard-library modules when they help the task. Rebuild a previous C program from its requirements, then compare the design. The first four exercises run with Python's standard library only.

quiz.explanation: Both names refer to the same list.

quiz.prompt: What is a useful first edge case for an average?
quiz.explanation: An empty collection makes an unchecked division by its length invalid.

tasks.title: Validate a batch of frequencies
tasks.brief: Accept multiple values and reject invalid entries without losing valid ones.
requirements: Read one line of whitespace-separated tokens.
Accept only finite nonnegative floats; reject negatives, nan, inf, and nonnumeric tokens.
Print each accepted value converted to MHz with three decimals and " MHz".
Finally print "Rejected: N" with the rejected count. An empty line rejects zero.
hints: Separate token parsing from numeric validation.
float can parse nan and inf, so conversion success is not enough.
The math standard library exposes isfinite; handle ValueError for text that is not numeric.
